name: Carbon
where: Cut down any plant, tree or fungal growth with the mining beam; available on every planet.
hidden: Running out strands you, because it fuels the very tool you mine with. Always keep a buffer before exploring far from your ship.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Condensed Carbon
where: Refine Carbon 2:1 in any refiner, or mine the red crystal clusters dotted across planet surfaces.
hidden: Burns much longer per inventory slot than raw Carbon and feeds countless recipes, so keep a stack even though it barely sells. (Wert unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Deuterium
where: Refine Tritium + Di-hydrogen, or Silicate Powder + Di-hydrogen, in a refiner; rarely found directly.
hidden: A refined fuel, not a raw find: making your own from cheap Di-hydrogen + Silicate Powder beats buying it. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Di-hydrogen
where: Mine the blue crystal formations scattered across every planet surface.
hidden: It fuels your launch thrusters; without it you cannot take off. Refine 5:1 into Di-hydrogen Jelly to store launch fuel compactly.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Ferrite Dust
where: Shoot any rocky boulder or terrain with the mining beam; found on practically every planet, moon and base.
hidden: It is the backbone of almost every build and craft. Never sell it; the few units it fetches are not worth the constant re-gathering.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Magnetised Ferrite
where: Refine Pure Ferrite together with a metal (Copper, Silver or Gold) in a refiner; occasionally found as surface deposits.
hidden: Only a handful of advanced parts need it, so make it on demand rather than hoarding and clogging inventory slots.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Oxygen
where: Harvest red-flagged plants on almost any planet, or buy it cheaply at most trade terminals.
hidden: It doubles as a refiner catalyst: feeding Oxygen into many recipes multiplies the output, so it is worth far more than its sell price suggests.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Pure Ferrite
where: Refine Ferrite Dust 1:1 in any refiner; also sold at construction and trade terminals.
hidden: You rarely need to mine for it: surplus Ferrite Dust converts for free in the refiner while you get on with other things.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Sodium
where: Harvest yellow-flagged plants, or grab the glowing yellow crystals on cliffs and in caves.
hidden: Recharges hazard protection instantly, even mid-storm; a cheap lifesaver beginners often ignore in favour of running for shelter.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Sodium Nitrate
where: Refine Sodium 2:1, or mine it directly as a deposit on some planets.
hidden: Restores far more protection per unit than raw Sodium, so refine a stack before heading to extreme-weather worlds.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Tritium
where: Shoot asteroids from your starship; interstellar belts are full of it. Watch for 'Tritium-Rich' asteroids and Hyperclusters (~100 each).
hidden: It refuels the pulse engine directly with no crafting. Outlaw stations always stock some, handy when an asteroid belt is far away.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Nitrogen
where: Build a Gas Extractor on a Nitrogen gas hotspot (locate one with the survey device), usually on Lush or Toxic worlds; also via Atmosphere Harvesters.
hidden: Cheap raw, but combined with Condensed Carbon it makes Nitrogen Salt, a step toward commodities worth hundreds of thousands. Keep it for crafting, not selling. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Radon
where: Gas Extractor on a Radon hotspot, found on Irradiated and Frozen worlds; also via Atmosphere Harvesters.
hidden: Turns into Enriched Carbon with Condensed Carbon; an automated extractor makes it near-free passive income. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Sulphurine
where: Gas Extractor on a Sulphurine hotspot, found on Scorched, Desert and Volcanic worlds.
hidden: Feeds the Thermic Condensate chain; a passive Gas Extractor farm quietly stockpiles it while you play elsewhere. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Ammonia
where: Dig the marked deposit nodes on Toxic planets with the terrain tool.
hidden: A key link in the very lucrative Stasis Device chain, so stock up on toxic worlds, which only appear occasionally in some regions.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Chlorine
where: Mine underwater crystal growths, or refine it from Salt.
hidden: Chlorine + Oxygen in a refiner yields MORE Chlorine than you put in. Loop it with cheap station-bought Oxygen to print millions. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Cobalt
where: Mine the glowing deposits inside caves on most planets; guaranteed in quantity on irradiated worlds.
hidden: Caves keep you safe from surface hazards, so you can farm Cobalt for ages. Refine it to Ionised Cobalt for a free value bump before selling.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Dioxite
uses: Crafting Cryogenic Chamber and cold-weather tech
where: Mine deposits on Frozen/icy planets.
hidden: Frozen-world locked; station traders sometimes sell it, but it is far easier to stock up whenever you land on snow.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Ionised Cobalt
uses: Ion Battery & Advanced Ion Battery crafting
where: Refine Cobalt 1:1, or buy Cobalt cheaply and refine it in bulk.
hidden: Crafting it into Ion Batteries multiplies its value again; a single Cobalt-rich cave becomes a tidy income stream this way.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Paraffinium
where: Harvest the yellow-flowering plants on Lush and warm worlds, or mine surface deposits.
hidden: Frequently needed for base parts; if your home planet lacks it, keep a supply from a lush world rather than hunting for it mid-build.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Phosphorus
where: Dig the marked deposit nodes on Scorched/fiery planets with the terrain tool.
hidden: Locked to hot worlds, so grab a stack whenever you visit one; a recipe needing it can catch you out far from a scorched system. (unsicher: Biom-Verteilung variiert je Update)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Pyrite
where: Mine deposits on desert and scorched worlds, or refine Gold together with Oxygen.
hidden: You can manufacture it in a refiner from Gold + Oxygen when no desert world is nearby, which beginners rarely realise.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Salt
where: Mine the bright deposits on ocean worlds and some dead/barren planets; check coasts and the seabed.
hidden: The entry point to the Chlorine money loop: refine Salt to Chlorine, then multiply Chlorine with Oxygen for huge profit. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Uranium
uses: Crafting Health Station, Megawatt Heater, Radiation Deflector, etc.
where: Mine Uranium deposits on Irradiated (green/yellow) worlds with the terrain tool; sometimes inside metal 'fingers'.
hidden: It can fuel launch thrusters as a cheap alternative to Di-hydrogen and feeds many early base/tech recipes, so don't dump it. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Activated Cadmium
where: Mine Activated Cadmium deposits in red-star systems.
hidden: Sell the activated version; the value jump over base Cadmium is large. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Activated Copper
where: Mine the rarer Activated Copper surface deposits in yellow-star systems.
hidden: Worth markedly more than plain Copper raw, so sell the activated form and keep ordinary Copper for refining. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Activated Emeril
where: Mine Activated Emeril deposits in green-star systems.
hidden: Roughly double the value of base Emeril; an automated extractor on a hotspot prints units passively. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Activated Indium
where: Mine Activated Indium deposits on blue-star planets.
hidden: The highest-value raw resource in the game; a large automated Activated Indium mine is the classic mid-game money machine.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Cadmium
where: Mine deposits on planets in red-star systems (needs a Cadmium Drive installed to warp there).
hidden: Higher up the colour chain than Copper, so it yields more Chromatic Metal per unit when refined with Gold or Silver. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Chromatic Metal
uses: Required by almost all technology crafting
where: Refine any stellar metal (Copper, Cadmium, Emeril, Indium, Quartzite) in a refiner.
hidden: Never sell it: nearly every tech component needs it, so keep a few hundred on hand. Higher-colour metals refine into far more of it.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Copper
where: Mine Copper deposits near Electromagnetic Hotspots in yellow-star systems (scan with the Analysis Visor).
hidden: The cheapest road to Chromatic Metal; refine it together with Silver and Gold to boost the conversion ratio dramatically.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Emeril
where: Mine deposits on planets in green-star systems (needs an Emeril Drive).
hidden: Refining Emeril with Gold/Silver gives a strong Chromatic Metal return; many players over-mine cheap Copper instead and miss this.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Indium
where: Mine deposits on planets in blue-star systems (needs an Indium Drive, the final colour drive).
hidden: Blue systems are the end of the colour-drive chain; once there, an extractor on an Indium hotspot gives serious passive income.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Quartzite
where: Mine Quartzite stellar-metal deposits; the exact star-colour association is uncertain.
hidden: An often-overlooked stellar metal; treat it like the coloured metals and refine toward Chromatic Metal. (unsicher: Quelle/Verwendung je Version)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Gold
uses: Electrical components and Warp Drive parts
Refiner catalyst that boosts Chromatic Metal output
where: Mine gold-flecked asteroids, dig Gold deposits in caves, or take it from defeated pirates.
hidden: Needed for Warp Drive and other key tech, so keep ~50 before selling surplus. As a refiner catalyst it boosts stellar-metal-to-Chromatic conversion.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Platinum
where: Mine Platinum-rich asteroids, or dig surface and cave deposits.
hidden: One of the best raw earners early and rarely needed for crafting, so sell freely. (unsicher: aktuelle Refining-Rezepte)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Silver
where: Mine Silver deposits in underground caves.
hidden: Less craft-critical than Gold, so sell the bulk and keep only ~50 for refining combos with stellar metals.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Cactus Flesh
where: Harvest Echinocactus plants on Desert worlds.
hidden: Surplus refines straight to Carbon, so it is rarely wasted even when you only wanted the units.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Cyto-Phosphate
uses: Crafting Glass, Condensed Carbon, Aquatic Crystal
where: Mine underwater flora with the mining beam; be careful, it can spawn Abyssal Horrors.
hidden: It fuels the Nautilon submarine, so stock up before deep dives; mining it can summon underwater predators. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Faecium
where: Best farmed from the Gutrot Flower crop (~25 every 4h); also drops from creatures and damaged machinery.
hidden: Mainly a cooking ingredient; multiply it by refining Mordite with Condensed Carbon when a recipe needs a lot. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Frost Crystal
where: Harvest Frostwort plants on Frozen worlds.
hidden: The cold-biome counterpart to Cactus Flesh and Star Bulb; handy for the cold-tech recipes you meet on icy worlds. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Fungal Mould
where: Harvest Fungal Clusters on Toxic worlds.
hidden: Shares the toxic biome with Ammonia, so combine the gathering runs. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Gamma Root
where: Harvest Gamma Weed plants on Radioactive worlds.
hidden: Pick it while mining Uranium on the same irradiated planet to save a separate trip. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Kelp Sac
where: Harvest Candle Kelp underwater; approaching it also tops up your exosuit oxygen.
hidden: Harvesting refills your dive oxygen, so it doubles as a diving aid; it cannot be farmed, only gathered. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Marrow Bulb
where: Harvest Cave Marrow growths inside caves on most planets; also refinable from Crystallised Helium.
hidden: Grows in the same caves as Cobalt, so grab both in one descent. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Mordite
where: Drops when you kill fauna; also from Mordite Root crops, organic rocks on scorched/desert worlds, and some marsh deposits.
hidden: Piles up automatically as you fight wildlife; low value, so refine spares to Carbon or cook with it rather than hauling it around. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Solanium
where: Harvest Solar Vine plants on Scorched worlds.
hidden: Gather it on the same trips you mine Phosphorus, since both sit on hot planets. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Star Bulb
where: Harvest Star Bramble plants, which grow in clusters on Lush worlds.
hidden: Dense clusters mean one short run fills a stack; refine to Paraffinium if needed, otherwise selling is usually quicker.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Gravitino Ball
where: Pick them up on Sentinel-heavy planets; each pickup instantly triggers a Sentinel alert.
hidden: Grabbing one always aggroes Sentinels, so fight, flee, or plant Gravitino Hosts to farm them safely. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Living Pearl
where: Found inside Armoured Clams deep underwater.
hidden: Interact slowly instead of attacking to take the pearl before the clam snaps shut. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Pugneum
where: Drops from destroyed Sentinels; larger Sentinel types drop more.
hidden: Stacks up naturally during Sentinel fights, so refine it instead of letting it sit unused. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Runaway Mould
where: Loot the small canisters inside abandoned buildings and some caches.
hidden: Nearly worthless to sell, but refines 5:1 into Nanites, an easy early way to bank upgrade currency. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Sac Venom
where: Destroy urchin-like creatures on land or underwater; also farmable via the Venom Urchin plant.
hidden: A planted Venom Urchin gives a steady supply without hunting. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Storm Crystal
where: On extreme-weather worlds, during a storm, scan with the Analysis Visor and dig up the marked crystal.
hidden: Worth a fortune each, but only spawns mid-storm exactly when hazard protection drains fastest, so bring Sodium Nitrate.
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Tainted Metal
where: Drops from Corrupted Sentinels on Dissonant planets (those with purple crystal formations).
hidden: Refines 1:2 into Nanites, an excellent rate, making Dissonant-planet fights a reliable nanite farm. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Basalt
where: Mine the stellar-metal-shaped deposits found on some planets.
hidden: Looks like a stellar-metal node but is its own localised element with limited uses, so treat it as a minor sell item. (unsicher: Verwendung je Version)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Crystallised Helium
uses: Refines into Ferrite Dust, Lithium, Sodium Nitrate, Uranium, etc.
where: Mine the large deposits on gas-giant worlds around purple stars (scan with the Analysis Visor).
hidden: A flexible refiner feedstock that converts into several scarce elements when a planet lacks them. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Lithium
uses: Refines into Crystallised Helium, Ferrite Dust, Kelp Sac, Pyrite, Sodium Nitrate
where: Mine deposits on Ocean worlds.
hidden: An ocean-world staple that refines into many scarce elements; stock up while diving for other water resources. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04

name: Silicate Powder
where: Dig soil with the terrain manipulator on any rocky world; extremely abundant.
hidden: Often grouped with valuables but actually low-value: keep it for building and for making Deuterium rather than selling. (Werte unsicher)
source: Paraphrased from NMS community wikis & guides, 2026-06-04
